sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface localization confirmed by immunofluorescence staining in K562 cells (L6); no functional assay reported in the ledger.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 name the stalk between EC6 and the TM helix as the Myc-tag insertion site for cPCDH constructs including αC1-related isoforms; L5 and L6 confirm that Pcdh-αC1 itself was tagged extracellularly and reached the cell surface. The stalk spans approximately residues 652–681 (extracellular domain ends at 681, TM begins at 682). No ledger line names a specific residue junction, so insert_after_residue is left null and the site is reported at region level. The stalk is well clear of the TM boundary and is the canonical extracellular tag position used across the cPCDH family. PMC4183217 (L5/L6) explicitly created extracellular c-Myc-tagged Pcdh-αC1 constructs by overlapping PCR and confirmed cell-surface localization by immunofluorescence in K562 cells. PMC12157453 (L1) and PMC12337331 (L2) further specify that for cPCDH constructs including αC1-related isoforms, the Myc tag was positioned in the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix, equivalently to previously validated constructs.

sources.claim: For derived constructs including the myc tag, the tag was positioned in the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix ( Figure S1A ), equivalently to previously validated constructs ( 21 ).

literature_notes: All six ledger lines converge on one site: the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix. L5/L6 (PMC4183217) are the strongest evidence, explicitly naming Pcdh-αC1 with a surface-confirmed extracellular Myc tag; L1/L2 (PMC12157453, PMC12337331) specify the stalk as the tag location for αC1-related cPCDH constructs. L3/L4 reference Myc-tagged αC2 as a validated paralog construct but add no new site. No ledger line names a specific residue, so the site is reported at region level (insert_after_residue null). No N-terminal tag evidence exists (the N-terminus carries a signal peptide and no ledger line reports a post-cleavage N-terminal tag for this protein). No intracellular or function-abrogating positions were reported in the ledger.
